pagetitle: "Healthcare · North Meck Insights"

```{r}
#| include: false
source("R/nm.R")
towns <- c("Cornelius", "Davidson", "Huntersville")

# Health insurance (ACS, one row per town per year)
ins <- nm_data("healthcare-insurance")
ins_years <- sort(unique(ins$year))
y_first <- min(ins_years); y_last <- max(ins_years)
i24 <- ins[ins$year == 2024, ]
i24 <- i24[match(towns, i24$Town), ]
nm_claim(identical(i24$Town, towns), "insurance text quotes 2024 figures for all three towns")
num_cols <- names(i24)[sapply(i24, is.numeric) & !names(i24) %in% c("year")]
tot <- colSums(i24[num_cols])                       # North Meck totals, 2024
rate <- function(u, i) tot[[u]] / (tot[[u]] + tot[[i]]) * 100   # uninsured share of a group

# Overview stat 1: working-age adults (35-64) among the uninsured
age_unins <- c("unins_U18", "unins_19_25", "unins_26_34", "unins_35_64", "unins_65_over")
share_3564 <- setNames(i24$unins_35_64 / i24$all_unins * 100, towns)
share_3564_all <- tot[["unins_35_64"]] / tot[["all_unins"]]
nm_claim(all(apply(i24[age_unins], 1, which.max) == 4), "overview stat says 35–64 is the largest uninsured age group in every town")
nm_claim(all(share_3564 >= 40 & share_3564 <= 60), "overview stat says about 1 in 2 uninsured residents in every town is 35–64")

# Overview stat 2: employer coverage
cov_types <- c("emp_based_ins", "dir_purchase_ins", "medicare_cov", "medicaid_cov", "tricare_cov", "VA_cov", "other_cov_type")
emp_share <- tot[["emp_based_ins"]] / tot[["all_ins"]]
nm_claim(all(apply(i24[cov_types], 1, which.max) == 1), "text says employer coverage is the most common source in all three towns")
nm_claim(all(apply(i24[cov_types], 1, function(v) v[1] >= 2 * sort(v, decreasing = TRUE)[2])), "overview stat says employer coverage is 'by far' the most common source")

# Overview stat 3: preventive care (CDC PLACES)
pc <- nm_data("cdc-preventive-care")
pc_avg <- tapply(pc$val, pc$measure, mean)
nm_claim(names(which.min(pc_avg)) == "Dental", "preventive-care stat says dental visits are the lowest measure")

# Dot chart callout: uninsured per 100 residents (same rounding as the chart)
unins_rate <- setNames(i24$all_unins / (i24$all_ins + i24$all_unins) * 100, towns)
nm_claim(names(which.min(unins_rate)) == "Davidson", "dot chart callout says Davidson has the lowest uninsured rate")
nm_claim(round(unins_rate[["Cornelius"]]) == round(unins_rate[["Huntersville"]]), "dot chart callout says Cornelius and Huntersville sit at the same rate per 100")
nm_claim(tot[["all_unins"]] >= 2000, "callouts say low uninsured rates still mean thousands of uninsured residents")

# Coverage-type callout (% of total population, as in the heatmap)
medicaid_pct <- setNames(i24$medicaid_cov / i24$Tot_pop * 100, towns)
unins_pop_pct <- setNames(i24$all_unins / i24$Tot_pop * 100, towns)
nm_claim(max(medicaid_pct) - min(medicaid_pct) < 2, "coverage-type callout says Medicaid enrollment is similar across towns")

# Income and age callouts (North Meck totals, 2024)
inc_low <- rate("no_ins_U25", "ins_U25")
inc_high <- (tot[["no_ins_75_100"]] + tot[["no_ins_100_above"]]) /
  (tot[["no_ins_75_100"]] + tot[["no_ins_100_above"]] + tot[["ins_75_100"]] + tot[["ins_100_above"]]) * 100
inc_ratio <- inc_low / inc_high
nm_claim(inc_ratio >= 2, "income callout says the under-$25k uninsured rate is several times the $75k+ rate")
age_rate <- c("Under 19" = rate("unins_U18", "ins_U18"), "19–25" = rate("unins_19_25", "ins_19_25"),
              "26–34" = rate("unins_26_34", "ins_26_34"), "35–64" = rate("unins_35_64", "ins_35_64"),
              "65+" = rate("unins_65_over", "ins_65_over"))
nm_claim(names(which.max(age_rate)) == "26–34", "age callout says 26–34 has the highest uninsured rate")
nm_claim(all(names(sort(age_rate, decreasing = TRUE))[1:2] %in% c("26–34", "35–64")), "coverage-gap intro says adults 26–64 carry the highest uninsured rates")
nm_claim(all(100 - age_rate[c("Under 19", "65+")] >= 95), "age callout says children and seniors have near-universal coverage")

# Trend callout: coverage by year
cov_by_year <- sapply(ins_years, function(y) { d <- ins[ins$year == y, ]; sum(d$all_ins) / sum(d$all_ins + d$all_unins) * 100 })
town_cov <- function(t, y) { d <- ins[ins$Town == t & ins$year == y, ]; d$all_ins / (d$all_ins + d$all_unins) * 100 }
nm_claim(all(sapply(ins_years, function(y) which.max(sapply(towns, town_cov, y = y)) == 2)), "trend callout says Davidson has led coverage every year")
cov_gain <- sapply(towns, function(t) town_cov(t, y_last) - town_cov(t, y_first))
nm_claim(cov_gain[["Huntersville"]] < cov_gain[["Cornelius"]], "trend callout says Huntersville improved more slowly than Cornelius")

# Employment callout
emp_cov <- 100 - rate("emp_uninsured", "emp_insured")
unemp_cov <- 100 - rate("unemp_uninsured", "unemp_insured")
nm_claim(100 - unemp_cov > max(inc_low, age_rate), "employment callout calls employment the strongest predictor: unemployed uninsured rate should top every income and age group")

# Mental health (CDC PLACES) and facility map
mh_dep <- nm_data("mh-depression")
mh_years <- sort(unique(mh_dep$year))
nm_claim(identical(mh_years, sort(unique(nm_data("mh-distress")$year))), "mental health cards list the same years for both charts")
fac <- nm_data("mental-health-facilities")
meck_cities <- c("Charlotte", "Cornelius", "Davidson", "Huntersville", "Matthews", "Mint Hill", "Pineville")
nm_claim(any(!fac$city %in% meck_cities), "facility map text says it covers Mecklenburg and surrounding counties")

# Chronic disease (CDC PLACES; static file, see data/cdc-chronic-disease.json)
cd <- nm_data("cdc-chronic-disease")
cd_years <- sort(unique(cd$year))
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
import {Plot, stdPlot, chips, townChips, responsive, loadData, TOWNS, FONT} from "/js/nm-charts.js"

insurance = loadData("healthcare-insurance")
prevCare = loadData("cdc-preventive-care")
mhDepression = loadData("mh-depression")
mhDistress = loadData("mh-distress")
chronic = loadData("cdc-chronic-disease")

// This page's own palettes, carried over from the original charts.
HC_TOWN_RANGE = ["#2E86AB", "#1B4F72", "#E8A838"]
INS_RANGE = ["#2E86AB", "#E8A838"]   // Insured, Uninsured
pctFmt = d => d + "%"

// 2024 rows in town order, and "All North Meck" as the sum of the three towns.
ins2024 = TOWNS.map(t => insurance.find(d => d.year === 2024 && d.Town === t))
SUM_COLS = Object.keys(insurance[0]).filter(k => !["GEOID", "Town", "year"].includes(k))
aggregate = rows => Object.fromEntries([["year", rows[0].year], ["Town", "All North Meck"], ...SUM_COLS.map(k => [k, d3.sum(rows, d => d[k] || 0)])])
singleRow = town => town === "All" ? aggregate(ins2024) : ins2024.find(d => d.Town === town)
trendRows = town => town === "All"
  ? [...new Set(insurance.map(d => d.year))].sort().map(y => aggregate(insurance.filter(d => d.year === y)))
  : insurance.filter(d => d.Town === town).sort((a, b) => a.year - b.year)

// A small bold title above a chart, like the in-SVG titles the original D3 charts drew.
withTitle = (text, node) => {
  const div = document.createElement("div");
  const t = document.createElement("div");
  t.textContent = text;
  t.style.cssText = "text-align:center;font:600 0.8rem 'Hanken Grotesk',sans-serif;color:#1B4F72;margin-bottom:6px";
  div.append(t, node);
  return div;
}

// Each age group's share of a town's uninsured residents (stacked to 100%).
AGES = ["Under 18", "19-25", "26-34", "35-64", "65+"]
AGE_COLS = ["unins_U18", "unins_19_25", "unins_26_34", "unins_35_64", "unins_65_over"]
ageShareChart = (width, {compact = false} = {}) => {
  const data = ins2024.flatMap(r => AGES.map((age, i) => ({town: r.Town, age, pct: r[AGE_COLS[i]] / r.all_unins * 100})));
  return stdPlot({
    width, height: compact ? 230 : 300, marginLeft: compact ? 78 : 100, marginBottom: compact ? 30 : 48,
    style: {...FONT, fontSize: compact ? "11px" : "12px"},
    x: {domain: [0, 100], ticks: [0, 25, 50, 75, 100], tickFormat: pctFmt, label: compact ? null : "Share of uninsured population (%)"},
    y: {domain: TOWNS, label: compact ? null : "Town"},
    color: {domain: AGES, range: ["#1A5276", "#2E86C1", "#85C1E9", "#F0A500", "#C0392B"], legend: true},
    marks: [
      Plot.barX(data, Plot.stackX({x: "pct", y: "town", fill: "age", order: AGES, tip: true,
        title: d => `${d.age}: ${d.pct.toFixed(1)}% of uninsured population`})),
      Plot.ruleX([0])
    ]
  });
}

// Insured vs. uninsured share for each group (one town or all of North Meck).
pairedBars = (groups, width, marginLeft) => {
  const data = groups.flatMap(g => [
    {label: g.label, status: "Insured", pct: g.ins},
    {label: g.label, status: "Uninsured", pct: 100 - g.ins}
  ]);
  return stdPlot({
    width, height: 320, marginLeft, marginTop: 10, marginBottom: 40,
    fy: {domain: groups.map(g => g.label), axis: "left", label: null, padding: 0.2, tickSize: 0},
    y: {domain: ["Insured", "Uninsured"], axis: null},
    x: {domain: [0, 100], ticks: 5, tickFormat: pctFmt, label: null},
    color: {domain: ["Insured", "Uninsured"], range: INS_RANGE, legend: true},
    marks: [
      Plot.barX(data, {fy: "label", y: "status", x: "pct", fill: "status", rx: 2, tip: true,
        title: d => `${d.label} · ${d.status}: ${d.pct.toFixed(1)}%`}),
      Plot.text(data.filter(d => d.pct > 4), {fy: "label", y: "status", x: "pct", text: d => d.pct.toFixed(1) + "%",
        dx: 3, textAnchor: "start", fontSize: 10, fill: "#555"})
    ]
  });
}
groupRate = (r, ins, unins) => ({ins: r[ins] / (r[ins] + r[unins]) * 100})

// Uninsured rate by age group for one row of insurance data.
trendRates = r => ({
  year: r.year,
  "Under 18": r.unins_U18 / (r.ins_U18 + r.unins_U18) * 100,
  "19-64": (r.unins_19_25 + r.unins_26_34 + r.unins_35_64) / (r.ins_19_25 + r.ins_26_34 + r.ins_35_64 + r.unins_19_25 + r.unins_26_34 + r.unins_35_64) * 100,
  "65+": r.unins_65_over / (r.ins_65_over + r.unins_65_over) * 100,
  "Total population": r.all_unins / (r.all_ins + r.all_unins) * 100
})

// Grouped prevalence bars with confidence intervals (CDC PLACES), used by the
// mental health and chronic disease charts. All towns: bars by year, one per
// town. One town: one bar per year, colored by year, with the value inside.
prevalenceChart = (rows, town, width, {yearColors, headroom = 1.18, labelDy = 80, xLabel = null}) => {
  const height = 280, mL = 54, mR = 20;
  const errorBars = (data, x, fx, capWidth) => [
    Plot.ruleX(data, {x, fx, y1: "lo", y2: "hi", stroke: "#333", strokeWidth: 1.5}),
    Plot.tickY(data, {x, fx, y: "hi", stroke: "#333", strokeWidth: 1.5, inset: capWidth}),
    Plot.tickY(data, {x, fx, y: "lo", stroke: "#333", strokeWidth: 1.5, inset: capWidth})
  ];
  const band = (range, n, p) => range / (n + p) * (1 - p);
  if (town === "All") {
    const years = [...new Set(rows.map(d => d.year))].sort();
    const bw = band(band(width - mL - mR, years.length, 0.25), TOWNS.length, 0.06);
    return stdPlot({
      width, height, marginLeft: mL, marginRight: mR, marginTop: 30, marginBottom: 40,
      fx: {domain: years, label: xLabel, tickFormat: String, padding: 0.25, axis: "bottom", tickSize: 0},
      x: {domain: TOWNS, axis: null, padding: 0.06},
      y: {domain: [0, d3.max(rows, d => d.hi) * headroom], grid: true, ticks: 5, tickFormat: pctFmt, label: null},
      color: {domain: TOWNS, range: HC_TOWN_RANGE, legend: true},
      marks: [
        Plot.barY(rows, {fx: "year", x: "town", y: "val", fill: "town", rx: 2, tip: true, title: d => `${d.town} ${d.year}: ${d.val}%`}),
        ...errorBars(rows, "town", "year", Math.max(0, (bw - 8) / 2))
      ]
    });
  }
  const data = rows.filter(d => d.town === town).sort((a, b) => a.year - b.year);
  const years = data.map(d => d.year);
  const pad = 0.38;
  const bw = band(width - mL - mR, years.length, pad);
  return stdPlot({
    width, height, marginLeft: mL, marginRight: mR, marginTop: 30, marginBottom: 40,
    x: {domain: years, tickFormat: String, padding: pad, label: xLabel ? `${xLabel} · ${town}` : null, tickSize: 0},
    y: {domain: [0, d3.max(data, d => d.hi) * headroom], grid: true, ticks: 5, tickFormat: pctFmt, label: null},
    color: {domain: years, range: yearColors},
    marks: [
      Plot.barY(data, {x: "year", y: "val", fill: "year", rx: 2, tip: true, title: d => `${d.year}: ${d.val}% (CI: ${d.lo}–${d.hi}%)`}),
      Plot.text(data, {x: "year", y: "val", text: d => d.val + "%", dy: labelDy, fill: "#fff", fontSize: 13, fontWeight: 500}),
      ...errorBars(data, "year", undefined, Math.max(0, (bw - 10) / 2))
    ]
  });
}
```

```{ojs}
{
  const TYPES = [
    {key: "emp_based_ins", label: "Employer-based"}, {key: "medicare_cov", label: "Medicare"},
    {key: "dir_purchase_ins", label: "Direct-purchase"}, {key: "medicaid_cov", label: "Medicaid"},
    {key: "other_cov_type", label: "Other"}, {key: "tricare_cov", label: "TRICARE"}, {key: "VA_cov", label: "VA"}
  ];
  // 2024 only: the dataset carries earlier years too, which must not be summed together.
  const scoped = ins2024.filter(d => masterTown === "All" || d.Town === masterTown);
  const data = TYPES.map(t => ({type: t.label, count: d3.sum(scoped, r => r[t.key] || 0)})).sort((a, b) => b.count - a.count);
  return responsive(width => stdPlot({
    width, height: 90 + data.length * 30, marginLeft: 130,
    x: {label: "Insured residents", grid: true},
    y: {label: null, domain: data.map(d => d.type)},
    marks: [
      Plot.barX(data, {x: "count", y: "type", fill: "#2E86AB", rx: 3, tip: true, title: d => `${d.type}\n${d.count.toLocaleString()} residents (2024)`}),
      Plot.ruleX([0])
    ]
  }), {invalidation});
}
```

```{ojs}
  const scoped = masterTown === "All" ? prevCare : prevCare.filter(d => d.town === masterTown);
```

<div class="tabpane" data-pane="hc-insurance">
<div class="wrap">
<div class="sec-head"><span class="eyebrow">Health Insurance</span><h2 class="sec-h">Who has coverage, and who is one medical bill away from a financial crisis?</h2><p class="lead">Insurance status is a primary driver of whether people seek preventive care or delay treatment until a condition becomes an emergency. In North Meck, income and employment type shape coverage more than geography alone.</p></div>
<!-- Dot chart: always all three towns; hidden while the coverage-type chart below shows a single town -->
<div id="hc-ins-dot-wrap" style="margin-bottom:36px">
<h3 style="font-family:'Newsreader',serif;font-size:22px;font-weight:400;margin-bottom:6px;color:var(--ink)">How many residents are uninsured?</h3>
<p style="color:var(--ink-2);font-size:15px;margin-bottom:16px">Each dot represents one person per 100 residents. Orange dots are uninsured.</p>
<div class="card viz-host" style="padding:24px 20px 16px">
<div class="card-t">Overall insurance coverage rate by town (2024)</div>
<div class="card-s">ACS 2024 · 1 dot = 1 person per 100 residents · all three towns</div>

<div id="hc-ins-dot" style="overflow-x:auto;margin-top:12px">

```{ojs}
responsive(width => {
  const DOT_TITLE_COLORS = {Cornelius: "#3f4e75", Davidson: "#f0a500", Huntersville: "#e05c4b"};
  const wrap = document.createElement("div");
  const row = document.createElement("div");
  row.style.cssText = "display:flex;justify-content:center;gap:" + Math.round(width * 0.05) + "px";
  const colW = Math.min(220, Math.floor((width - 2 * Math.round(width * 0.05)) / 3));
  const step = colW / 10;
  for (const r of ins2024) {
    const pct = r.all_unins / (r.all_ins + r.all_unins) * 100;
    const n = Math.round(pct);
    const dots = d3.range(100).map(i => ({col: i % 10, row: Math.floor(i / 10), status: i >= 100 - n ? "Uninsured" : "Insured"}));
    const col = document.createElement("div");
    col.style.cssText = "text-align:center;font-family:'Hanken Grotesk',sans-serif";
    col.innerHTML = `<div style="font-size:13px;font-weight:600;color:${DOT_TITLE_COLORS[r.Town]}">${r.Town}</div>` +
      `<div style="font-size:10px;color:#888">${n} of 100 uninsured</div>`;
    col.append(Plot.plot({
      width: colW, height: colW, margin: step / 2, style: FONT,
      x: {domain: d3.range(10), axis: null, type: "point"}, y: {domain: d3.range(10), axis: null, type: "point"},
      color: {domain: ["Insured", "Uninsured"], range: INS_RANGE},
      marks: [Plot.dot(dots, {x: "col", y: "row", fill: "status", r: step * 0.35, tip: true,
        title: d => `${r.Town} · ${d.status}${d.status === "Uninsured" ? ` · ${pct.toFixed(1)}% uninsured` : ""}`})]
    }));
    row.append(col);
  }
  const legend = Plot.legend({color: {domain: ["Insured", "Uninsured"], range: INS_RANGE}, style: {...FONT, fontSize: "11px"}});
  legend.style.cssText += ";display:flex;justify-content:center;margin-top:10px";
  wrap.append(row, legend);
  return wrap;
}, {invalidation})
```

</div>

</div>
<div class="nm-callout info" style="margin-top:16px"><div class="nm-callout-t">Davidson has the lowest uninsured rate in North Meck — roughly `r round(unins_rate[["Davidson"]])` in 100 residents lack coverage — while Cornelius and Huntersville each sit around `r round(unins_rate[["Cornelius"]])` in 100. Even these low rates represent thousands of residents without a safety net for medical emergencies.</div><div class="nm-callout-s">Source: <span class="gloss-link" data-term="acs" role="button" tabindex="0" onclick="glossTerm('acs')">ACS</span> 2024</div></div>

```{ojs}
viewof incomeTown = townChips(masterTown, {all: "All", label: ""})
{
  const BRACKETS = [["Below $25k", "U25"], ["$25k-$50k", "25_50"], ["$50k-$75k", "50_75"], ["$75k-$100k", "75_100"], ["Above $100k", "100_above"]];
  if (incomeTown !== "All") {
    const r = singleRow(incomeTown);
    const labels = ["Under $25k", "$25k–$50k", "$50k–$75k", "$75k–$100k", "Above $100k"];
    const groups = BRACKETS.map(([, k], i) => ({label: labels[i], ...groupRate(r, "ins_" + k, "no_ins_" + k)}));
    return responsive(width => pairedBars(groups, width, 105), {invalidation});
  }
  const brackets = BRACKETS.map(b => b[0]);
  const data = ins2024.flatMap(r => BRACKETS.map(([b, k]) => ({town: r.Town, bracket: b, value: r["no_ins_" + k] / (r["ins_" + k] + r["no_ins_" + k]) * 100})));
  const yMax = d3.max(data, d => d.value) * 1.2;
  const zeros = data.filter(d => d.value === 0);
  return responsive(width => withTitle("Uninsurance Rates by Income Bracket, North Mecklenburg 2024", stdPlot({
    width, height: 330, marginLeft: 60, marginBottom: 55,
    fx: {domain: brackets, label: "Income bracket", axis: "bottom", padding: 0.2, tickSize: 0},
    x: {domain: TOWNS, axis: null, padding: 0.05},
    y: {domain: [0, yMax], grid: true, label: "Uninsured rate (%)", tickFormat: pctFmt},
    color: {domain: TOWNS, range: ["#1A5276", "#F0A500", "#C0392B"], legend: true},
    marks: [
      Plot.barY(data, {fx: "bracket", x: "town", y: "value", fill: "town", rx: 1, tip: true, title: d => `${d.town} (${d.bracket}): ${d.value.toFixed(1)}% uninsured`}),
      // Point out bars that are zero-height, so a 0% reads as data rather than a gap.
      Plot.arrow(zeros, {fx: "bracket", x1: "town", x2: "town", y1: yMax * 0.14, y2: yMax * 0.02, stroke: "#1B4F72", strokeWidth: 1.5, headLength: 6}),
      Plot.text(zeros, {fx: "bracket", x: "town", y: yMax * 0.14, text: d => `0% (${d.town})`, dy: -7, fontSize: 11, fill: "#1B4F72"}),
      Plot.ruleY([0])
    ]
  })), {invalidation});
}
```

```{ojs}
viewof ageTrendTown = townChips(masterTown, {label: ""})
{
  const years = [...new Set(insurance.map(d => d.year))].sort();
  const panel = (title, data, colorDomain, colorRange, width, height, extra = {}) => stdPlot({
    width, height, marginLeft: 56, marginTop: 16, marginBottom: 44, ...extra,
    x: {type: "point", domain: years, padding: 0.5, label: "Year", labelOffset: 36, tickFormat: String},
    y: {domain: [0, d3.max(data, d => d.value) * 1.2], grid: true, ticks: 5, tickFormat: pctFmt, label: "Uninsured rate (%)"},
    color: {domain: colorDomain, range: colorRange},
    marks: [
      Plot.line(data, {x: "year", y: "value", stroke: "key", strokeWidth: 2.5}),
      Plot.dot(data, {x: "year", y: "value", fill: "key", r: extra.dotR || 3.5, tip: true, title: d => `${d.key} · ${d.group} (${d.year}): ${d.value.toFixed(1)}%`}),
      ...(extra.marks || [])
    ]
  });
  if (ageTrendTown === "All") {
    const GROUPS = ["Under 18", "19-64", "65+", "Total population"];
    const PANEL_TITLES = ["Under 18", "19-64", "65+", "Total Population"];
    const COLORS = ["#2a78d6", "#1baf7a", "#eda100"];
    const rows = insurance.flatMap(r => { const t = trendRates(r); return GROUPS.map(g => ({key: r.Town, group: g, year: r.year, value: t[g]})); });
    return responsive(width => {
      const wrap = document.createElement("div");
      const legend = Plot.legend({color: {domain: TOWNS, range: COLORS}, style: {...FONT, fontSize: "12px"}});
      legend.style.cssText += ";display:flex;justify-content:center;margin-bottom:10px";
      const grid = document.createElement("div");
      grid.style.cssText = "display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(2,1fr);gap:16px";
      const pw = Math.floor((width - 16) / 2);
      GROUPS.forEach((g, i) => {
        const cell = document.createElement("div");
        const t = document.createElement("div");
        t.textContent = PANEL_TITLES[i];
        t.style.cssText = "text-align:center;font:600 0.85rem 'Hanken Grotesk',sans-serif;color:#1B4F72";
        cell.append(t, panel(g, rows.filter(d => d.group === g), TOWNS, COLORS, pw, 230));
        grid.append(cell);
      });
      wrap.append(legend, grid);
      return wrap;
    }, {invalidation});
  }
  const GROUPS = ["Under 18", "19-64", "65+", "Total population"];
  const COLORS = ["#2E86AB", "#1B4F72", "#E8A838", "#7B7D7D"];
  const rows = trendRows(ageTrendTown).flatMap(r => { const t = trendRates(r); return GROUPS.map(g => ({key: g, group: ageTrendTown, year: r.year, value: t[g]})); });
  // Line-end labels, nudged apart so they don't overlap.
  const height = 420, innerH = height - 40 - 50, yMax = d3.max(rows, d => d.value) * 1.2;
  const ends = GROUPS.map(g => rows.filter(d => d.key === g).at(-1)).sort((a, b) => b.value - a.value);
  const gap = 14 / innerH * yMax;
  ends.forEach((d, i) => { d.labelY = i && ends[i - 1].labelY - d.value < gap ? ends[i - 1].labelY - gap : d.value; });
  return responsive(width => panel(ageTrendTown, rows, GROUPS, COLORS, width, height, {
    marginTop: 40, marginRight: 110, marginBottom: 50, dotR: 4,
    marks: [Plot.text(ends, {x: "year", y: "labelY", text: "key", fill: "key", dx: 8, textAnchor: "start", fontSize: 12})]
  }), {invalidation});
}
```

```{ojs}
responsive(width => prevalenceChart(mhDepression, depressionTown, width, {yearColors: ["#C0392B", "#1A7A7A", "#E67E22"]}), {invalidation})
```

<!-- TAB: chronic disease -->
<div class="tabpane" data-pane="hc-chronic">
<div class="wrap">
<div class="sec-head"><span class="eyebrow">Chronic Disease &amp; Prevention</span><h2 class="sec-h">How much chronic disease burden does North Meck carry, and is it preventable?</h2><p class="lead">Diabetes, obesity, and hypertension are among the most prevalent and costly chronic conditions in the United States. Their rates are shaped by income, food access, housing stability, and stress — making them direct downstream indicators of the social determinants this portal tracks.</p></div>
<!-- Section 1: Chronic disease metric charts -->
<div style="margin-bottom:36px">
<h3 style="font-family:'Newsreader',serif;font-size:22px;font-weight:400;margin-bottom:6px;color:var(--ink)">How do diabetes, obesity, and hypertension rates compare across towns?</h3>
<p style="color:var(--ink-2);font-size:15px;margin-bottom:16px"><span class="gloss-link" data-term="age-adjusted" role="button" tabindex="0" onclick="glossTerm('age-adjusted')">Age-adjusted</span> <span class="gloss-link" data-term="prevalence" role="button" tabindex="0" onclick="glossTerm('prevalence')">prevalence</span> estimates from <span class="gloss-link" data-term="places" role="button" tabindex="0" onclick="glossTerm('places')">CDC PLACES</span> (`r paste(cd_years, collapse = ", ")`), allowing trend comparison within and between towns.</p>

```{ojs}
//| output: false
chronicChart = (measure, width) => prevalenceChart(chronic.filter(d => d.measure === measure), masterTown, width,
  {yearColors: HC_TOWN_RANGE, headroom: masterTown === "All" ? 1.18 : 1.2, labelDy: 83, xLabel: "Year"})
```

<div class="g2" style="margin-bottom:20px">

<h3 style="font-family:'Newsreader',serif;font-size:22px;font-weight:400;margin-bottom:6px;color:var(--ink)">Are high-chronic-disease areas the same as high-cost-burden areas?</h3>
<p style="color:var(--ink-2);font-size:15px;margin-bottom:16px">Chronic disease and housing cost burden often overlap — residents under financial stress are less likely to maintain preventive care, take medications consistently, or avoid high-stress environments that worsen chronic conditions.</p>
